This variant applies Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) as auto-encoders for voxel-based mapping, specifically in the context of robotics and dense TSDF space mapping [S1]. **Parameters:** The network architecture consists of 4096, 512, $d$, 512, 4096 nodes, where $d$ is the descriptor dimension [S1].

Unlike linear transforms, these methods adapt to the specific statistical structure of the data, though empirical results on voxel mapping show that linear methods like PCA can still yield lower reconstruction error than neural network autoencoders [S1].

Implementation utilizes cuBLAS and Thrust libraries for GPU computation [S1]. **Performance:** For an ANN with 128 latent dimensions (NN 128), the Mean Squared Error (MSE) reconstruction error is $45.66 \pm 4.25$, and the Mean Absolute Trajectory Error (ATE) is $0.13 \pm 0.20$ m [S1]. **Comparison:** ANN encoders yield worse reconstruction fidelity than PCA encoders (e.g., PCA 128 MSE is $26.88 \pm 2.57$), but AE compression results in better pose estimation (lower ATE) than PCA [S1].
